title: AutoGen: Enabling Next-Gen LLM Applications via Multi-Agent Conversation
chunk_text: AutoGen is an open-source framework for building LLM applications using multiple conversational agents. Agents can be customized, composed, and made to interact with each other and humans. The framework enables diverse conversation patterns, including hierarchical chats, joint problem-solving, and feedback-driven iterative refinement.

title: AutoGen: Enabling Next-Gen LLM Applications via Multi-Agent Conversation
chunk_text: The emergence of large language models has created new opportunities for building intelligent applications. However, single-agent systems face fundamental limitations in complex reasoning and multi-step task execution. We propose AutoGen, a framework where multiple LLM-powered agents collaborate through structured conversation. Each agent has a defined role, and agents communicate by passing messages. This allows decomposing complex problems across specialized agents.

title: AutoGen: Enabling Next-Gen LLM Applications via Multi-Agent Conversation
chunk_text: AutoGen demonstrates that multi-agent conversation is a practical and scalable paradigm for LLM applications. Across diverse benchmarks including math reasoning, code generation, and question answering, AutoGen outperforms single-agent baselines. Future directions include dynamic agent creation and better handling of conflicting agent outputs.

title: CAMEL: Communicative Agents for Mind Exploration of Large Language Model Society
chunk_text: CAMEL proposes a role-playing framework where two LLM agents adopt complementary roles to collaboratively solve tasks. The key innovation is inception prompting, which guides agents to complete tasks while maintaining role coherence without human intervention.

title: CAMEL: Communicative Agents for Mind Exploration of Large Language Model Society
chunk_text: We investigate role-playing as a mechanism for multi-agent collaboration in LLMs. In CAMEL, an AI user agent provides instructions to an AI assistant agent, creating a structured directive conversation. Inception prompting embeds task context into both agents system prompts to prevent role deviation. We study emergent social behaviors across 50 domains and 20 languages.

title: CAMEL: Communicative Agents for Mind Exploration of Large Language Model Society
chunk_text: Role-playing enables structured, coherent multi-agent dialogue without human oversight. CAMEL successfully completes tasks across coding, mathematics, and science domains. We observe emergent phenomena including role flipping and task abandonment. These failure modes present important challenges for future work.

title: Reflexion: Language Agents with Verbal Reinforcement Learning
chunk_text: Reflexion reinforces language agents through verbal feedback rather than weight updates. An agent reflects on task feedback using natural language, converting binary rewards into detailed verbal summaries stored in episodic memory. This verbal memory informs future task attempts without model fine-tuning.

title: Reflexion: Language Agents with Verbal Reinforcement Learning
chunk_text: Reinforcement learning for language agents traditionally requires expensive gradient updates. We propose Reflexion, where an agent learns from mistakes by generating natural language self-reflections stored in episodic memory. These reflections are prepended to future attempts, enabling the agent to learn from failure without weight updates.

title: Reflexion: Language Agents with Verbal Reinforcement Learning
chunk_text: Reflexion achieves state-of-the-art performance on HumanEval, WebArena, and AlfWorld without modifying model weights. Verbal reinforcement provides a practical alternative to gradient-based RL. Key limitations include the context window constraint on episodic memory depth.

title: MetaGPT: Meta Programming for A Multi-Agent Collaborative Framework
chunk_text: MetaGPT assigns specialized roles to multiple GPT agents who collaborate on software development tasks. It incorporates software engineering workflow conventions into agent interactions to improve coordination and output quality through structured role specialization.

title: MetaGPT: Meta Programming for A Multi-Agent Collaborative Framework
chunk_text: Existing multi-agent frameworks lack structured coordination protocols. MetaGPT draws inspiration from software engineering practices, assigning standardized roles and communication channels to agents. This structured approach reduces inconsistencies and improves task completion rates on software development benchmarks.

title: MetaGPT: Meta Programming for A Multi-Agent Collaborative Framework
chunk_text: MetaGPT demonstrates that incorporating human organizational structures into multi-agent systems significantly improves performance. Role specialization and structured communication are key factors in successful multi-agent collaboration on engineering tasks.

title: AgentBench: Evaluating LLMs as Agents
chunk_text: AgentBench is a comprehensive benchmark for evaluating LLMs as autonomous agents across eight distinct environments including operating systems, web browsing, databases, and card games. It measures multi-step reasoning, tool use, and long-horizon task completion across 27 LLMs.

title: AgentBench: Evaluating LLMs as Agents
chunk_text: The rapid development of LLM-based agents lacks standardized evaluation. Existing benchmarks focus on isolated capabilities rather than integrated agent behavior. AgentBench tests agents on realistic tasks requiring planning, tool use, and multi-step execution. We find significant performance gaps between commercial and open-source models.

title: AgentBench: Evaluating LLMs as Agents
chunk_text: AgentBench reveals that current LLMs struggle with long-horizon agent tasks, particularly in environments requiring precise tool use and state tracking. Commercial models significantly outperform open-source alternatives. We release the benchmark publicly to support the research community.

title: ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models
chunk_text: ReAct interleaves chain-of-thought reasoning traces with task-specific actions, enabling LLMs to reason about what to do, act to gather information, and update reasoning based on observations. ReAct outperforms reasoning-only and acting-only baselines on question answering, fact verification, and interactive decision-making tasks.

title: ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models
chunk_text: Existing approaches separate reasoning and acting in language models. We propose ReAct, which combines both: the model generates a Thought about the current state, takes an Action, and receives an Observation. This loop enables dynamic context updating, self-correction through grounded observations, and reduces hallucination compared to reasoning-only approaches.

title: ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models
chunk_text: ReAct achieves strong performance on HotpotQA, FEVER, ALFWorld, and WebShop. Grounding reasoning in real environment feedback reduces hallucination and improves task completion. ReAct-style reasoning-acting loops have since become the foundation for most modern LLM agent architectures.

title: Self-Refine: Iterative Refinement with Self-Feedback
chunk_text: Self-Refine enables a single LLM to iteratively generate output, critique that output, and refine it based on self-feedback. Without additional training or supervision, Self-Refine improves performance on code optimization, math reasoning, constrained generation, and sentiment reversal tasks.

title: Self-Refine: Iterative Refinement with Self-Feedback
chunk_text: Quality outputs often require iteration: draft, review, and revise. We propose Self-Refine, where one LLM plays generator, critic, and refiner in sequence. The model first generates an output, then critiques it by identifying weaknesses, then revises based on the critique. This iterative loop runs until a stopping condition is met without requiring separate training data.

title: Self-Refine: Iterative Refinement with Self-Feedback
chunk_text: Self-Refine improves output quality across 7 tasks using the same base model and no additional training. Largest gains appear where feedback is precise and measurable. A key limitation is that self-feedback quality is bounded by the model's capability ceiling on that task.

title: Generative Agents: Interactive Simulacra of Human Behavior
chunk_text: Generative agents simulate believable human behavior by combining LLMs with memory, reflection, and planning modules. Twenty-five agents in a sandbox environment exhibit emergent social behaviors including forming relationships, coordinating group activities, and spreading information through social networks.

title: Generative Agents: Interactive Simulacra of Human Behavior
chunk_text: Creating agents that behave believably as humans requires reasoning about the current situation, retrieving relevant memories, and planning future actions. Generative agents maintain a memory stream of experiences, synthesize reflective insights, and use retrieved context to plan. The architecture extends LLMs with structured memory supporting retrieval by recency, importance, and relevance.

title: Generative Agents: Interactive Simulacra of Human Behavior
chunk_text: Generative agents produce convincingly human-like behaviors in simulated social environments. Ablation studies confirm that memory, reflection, and planning are each essential. The work demonstrates LLM agents can sustain coherent behavior over extended time horizons, opening possibilities for interactive simulation and social AI research.

title: Voyager: An Open-Ended Embodied Agent with Large Language Models
chunk_text: Voyager is an LLM-powered embodied lifelong learning agent in Minecraft that continuously explores the world, acquires skills, and makes discoveries without human intervention. It uses an automatic curriculum for exploration, a growing skill library of executable code, and iterative prompting with environment feedback for self-improvement.

title: Voyager: An Open-Ended Embodied Agent with Large Language Models
chunk_text: Lifelong learning in open-ended environments requires autonomous goal-setting, skill acquisition, and adaptation. Voyager uses GPT-4 to propose exploration goals, write executable Minecraft bot programs, and refine those programs based on execution feedback. Successful programs enter a growing skill library enabling compound skill composition over time.

title: Voyager: An Open-Ended Embodied Agent with Large Language Models
chunk_text: Voyager discovers more unique items, achieves higher tech-tree progression, and shows better generalization to novel biomes than prior methods. The skill library enables knowledge transfer across tasks. Voyager establishes a new paradigm for open-ended embodied agent learning driven by code generation and execution feedback.

title: Communicative Agents for Software Development
chunk_text: ChatDev uses multiple LLM agents in organizational roles (CEO, CTO, programmer, tester, reviewer) collaborating through structured chat phases to develop software from natural language specifications. The framework divides development into designing, coding, testing, and documenting phases with defined consensus requirements.

title: Communicative Agents for Software Development
chunk_text: Software development requires diverse expertise and careful coordination. ChatDev simulates a software company using LLM agents in organizational roles. Agents communicate through structured chat sessions following a waterfall-inspired development process. Each phase has defined entry and exit criteria, requiring agents to reach consensus before proceeding.

title: Communicative Agents for Software Development
chunk_text: ChatDev successfully develops functional software from natural language requirements. Role-based coordination reduces hallucination compared to single-agent baselines. Structured phase transitions are critical for maintaining project coherence, and role conflicts are identified as a key failure mode requiring future work.

title: Toolformer: Language Models Can Teach Themselves to Use Tools
chunk_text: Toolformer trains language models to decide which tools to use, when, and with what arguments in a self-supervised manner. The model generates candidate API calls, executes them, and retains those that reduce perplexity on subsequent tokens. Toolformer achieves strong performance on QA, arithmetic, and search tasks without task-specific supervision.

title: Toolformer: Language Models Can Teach Themselves to Use Tools
chunk_text: Language models struggle with tasks requiring current information, precise arithmetic, or factual lookup. We train Toolformer to use external tools via self-supervised data generation: the model inserts candidate API calls, executes them, and keeps those that help predict the continuation. This requires no human annotation and generalizes across tool types.

title: Toolformer: Language Models Can Teach Themselves to Use Tools
chunk_text: Toolformer shows language models can learn effective tool use from self-supervised data. The approach generalizes across calculator, calendar, Wikipedia, and QA APIs. A key limitation is brittleness for novel tool types where the model cannot generate useful candidate calls.

title: HuggingGPT: Solving AI Tasks with ChatGPT and its Friends in HuggingFace
chunk_text: HuggingGPT uses ChatGPT as a task planner that selects specialized AI models from HuggingFace to solve complex user requests. ChatGPT decomposes tasks into sub-tasks, identifies the best model from model card descriptions, executes models sequentially, and integrates results into a final response enabling multimodal task solving.

title: HuggingGPT: Solving AI Tasks with ChatGPT and its Friends in HuggingFace
chunk_text: Complex AI tasks often require chaining multiple specialized models. HuggingGPT uses an LLM as a controller to orchestrate specialized models: parsing user intent, planning sub-tasks, selecting appropriate models from their descriptions, and synthesizing outputs. This enables solving multimodal tasks beyond any single model's capability.

title: HuggingGPT: Solving AI Tasks with ChatGPT and its Friends in HuggingFace
chunk_text: HuggingGPT handles diverse multimodal tasks by composing specialized models through LLM-based planning. The approach is flexible and extensible as new models become available on HuggingFace. Key challenges include latency from multiple model calls and sensitivity to model description quality for selection.

title: Chain-of-Thought Prompting Elicits Reasoning in Large Language Models
chunk_text: Chain-of-thought prompting improves LLM reasoning by providing exemplars with intermediate reasoning steps. This technique substantially improves performance on arithmetic, commonsense, and symbolic reasoning tasks, with the ability emerging only above a scale threshold.

title: Chain-of-Thought Prompting Elicits Reasoning in Large Language Models
chunk_text: Large language models often fail at multi-step reasoning tasks. Chain-of-thought prompting augments few-shot exemplars with reasoning chains before the final answer, encouraging step-by-step decomposition. Instead of mapping directly from question to answer, the model generates intermediate reasoning steps that guide the final response.

title: Chain-of-Thought Prompting Elicits Reasoning in Large Language Models
chunk_text: Chain-of-thought prompting dramatically improves performance on GSM8K, SVAMP, AQuA, and symbolic reasoning benchmarks. The technique is most effective above 100B parameters and for tasks benefiting from multi-step decomposition. Chain-of-thought is now a foundational technique for reasoning in LLM applications and agent design.

title: Tree of Thoughts: Deliberate Problem Solving with Large Language Models
chunk_text: Tree of Thoughts generalizes chain-of-thought by allowing LLMs to explore multiple reasoning paths as a tree, using the model itself to evaluate intermediate states and guide search via breadth-first or depth-first strategies. ToT substantially improves over chain-of-thought on tasks requiring search, planning, and backtracking.

title: Tree of Thoughts: Deliberate Problem Solving with Large Language Models
chunk_text: Chain-of-thought restricts reasoning to a single left-to-right path, preventing backtracking and exploration. Tree of Thoughts frames problem solving as tree search: the LLM proposes multiple candidate thoughts, evaluates which are most promising, and explores the best branches. This enables deliberate lookahead, backtracking, and reconsideration.

title: Tree of Thoughts: Deliberate Problem Solving with Large Language Models
chunk_text: ToT outperforms chain-of-thought and self-consistency on Game of 24, Creative Writing, and Mini Crosswords. The key contribution is enabling deliberate search using the LLM as both generator and evaluator. The approach is computationally more expensive but solves problems requiring systematic exploration that chain-of-thought cannot.

title: OpenAgents: An Open Platform for Language Agents in the Wild
chunk_text: OpenAgents is an open platform with three specialized agents for data analysis, web browsing, and third-party plugin integration supporting 200+ tools. Designed for real-world non-expert users, it provides a full-stack implementation including web interface, backend, and cloud services.

title: OpenAgents: An Open Platform for Language Agents in the Wild
chunk_text: Most LLM agent research evaluates on benchmarks without production deployment infrastructure. OpenAgents hosts three production-ready agents accessible via web interface: a Data Agent for analytical tasks, a Plugins Agent for external API integration, and a Web Agent for autonomous browsing. All agents log reasoning and actions for transparency and analysis.

title: OpenAgents: An Open Platform for Language Agents in the Wild
chunk_text: OpenAgents demonstrates LLM agents can be deployed at scale for diverse real-world tasks. Analysis of user interactions reveals common failure modes including ambiguous instructions, API errors, and context length limits. The platform contributes infrastructure, interaction logs, and analysis enabling reproducible research on deployed language agents.

title: SwiftSage: A Generative Agent with Fast and Slow Thinking for Complex Interactive Tasks
chunk_text: SwiftSage combines a small fine-tuned model for fast reactive decisions with a large LLM for slow deliberate planning, inspired by dual-process theory. The SWIFT module handles routine subtasks while SAGE handles novel or complex situations requiring reasoning, achieving better efficiency-capability tradeoffs than homogeneous designs.

title: SwiftSage: A Generative Agent with Fast and Slow Thinking for Complex Interactive Tasks
chunk_text: LLM agents either use a large model for all decisions (expensive) or a small model (limited). Dual-process theory suggests humans use fast System 1 and slow System 2 thinking. SwiftSage implements this: a fine-tuned small model (SWIFT) executes common action sequences while GPT-4 (SAGE) provides high-level planning when SWIFT is uncertain or the task is novel.

title: SwiftSage: A Generative Agent with Fast and Slow Thinking for Complex Interactive Tasks
chunk_text: SwiftSage outperforms large-model-only and small-model-only baselines on ScienceWorld interactive tasks. The dual-process architecture reduces API costs significantly while maintaining competitive performance. The work demonstrates that heterogeneous model combinations achieve better efficiency-capability tradeoffs than homogeneous agent designs.

title: WebGPT: Browser-Assisted Question-Answering with Human Feedback
chunk_text: WebGPT is a fine-tuned language model that uses a text-based web browser to answer long-form questions with citations. The model learns to search the web, navigate results, and synthesize information through imitation learning and reinforcement learning from human feedback, producing answers preferred by human evaluators.

title: WebGPT: Browser-Assisted Question-Answering with Human Feedback
chunk_text: Answering complex questions accurately requires current information synthesis from multiple sources. WebGPT trains with a simplified text-based browser, issuing search queries, clicking links, and scrolling pages. Training combines imitation learning on human demonstrations with reinforcement learning from human preference comparisons over answer quality.

title: WebGPT: Browser-Assisted Question-Answering with Human Feedback
chunk_text: WebGPT produces more factual, better-cited answers than GPT-3 baselines on ELI5 and TriviaQA. Human evaluators prefer WebGPT answers over human references on ELI5. The work demonstrates that tool use combined with human feedback training substantially improves factuality and groundedness in long-form question answering.

title: ToolLLM: Facilitating Large Language Models to Master 16000+ Real-World APIs
chunk_text: ToolLLM presents ToolBench, a benchmark covering 16000+ real-world APIs from 49 categories for training and evaluating LLM tool use at scale. A depth-first search decision tree evaluates multi-step tool use. Fine-tuned ToolLLaMA achieves competitive performance with ChatGPT on real-world API tasks.

title: ToolLLM: Facilitating Large Language Models to Master 16000+ Real-World APIs
chunk_text: Existing tool-use benchmarks cover few APIs and do not reflect real-world diversity. We construct ToolBench from RapidAPI Hub, generating instruction-API call pairs via ChatGPT. A depth-first search with backtracking decision tree captures multi-step API use better than simple success metrics, more accurately reflecting real-world tool use complexity.

title: ToolLLM: Facilitating Large Language Models to Master 16000+ Real-World APIs
chunk_text: ToolLLaMA generalizes to unseen APIs and multi-tool scenarios after fine-tuning on ToolBench. The benchmark reveals LLMs struggle with API parameter formatting, error recovery, and multi-tool coordination. ToolBench provides a reproducible platform for advancing tool-augmented language model research at scale.

title: A Survey on Large Language Model based Autonomous Agents
chunk_text: This survey reviews LLM-based autonomous agent research using a unified framework covering agent profile, memory, planning, and action components. Reviewing 150+ papers, it identifies open challenges in long-term planning, multi-agent coordination, safety, and evaluation methodology.

title: A Survey on Large Language Model based Autonomous Agents
chunk_text: LLM-based autonomous agents have emerged rapidly but lack a unified conceptual framework. We survey agent architectures through four core components: profile (agent role and persona), memory (information storage and retrieval), planning (goal decomposition and sequencing), and action (tool and environment interaction). We trace the evolution from simple prompted agents to complex multi-agent systems.

title: A Survey on Large Language Model based Autonomous Agents
chunk_text: LLM-based agents have achieved results across software development, web navigation, scientific discovery, and social simulation. Key challenges remain: long-horizon planning is unreliable, multi-agent coordination produces emergent failures, safety is underexplored, and benchmarks are fragmented. These are identified as the highest-priority open problems for the field.

title: TaskMatrix.AI: Completing Tasks by Connecting Foundation Models with Millions of APIs
chunk_text: TaskMatrix.AI connects foundation models with a large collection of APIs to complete both digital and physical tasks. A conversational model serves as task planner, selecting and invoking APIs from a registry. The system is evaluated on PowerPoint automation, image generation, and robot manipulation tasks.

title: TaskMatrix.AI: Completing Tasks by Connecting Foundation Models with Millions of APIs
chunk_text: Foundation models have strong language understanding but limited ability to take real-world actions. TaskMatrix.AI pairs a foundation model with an Action Executor that calls registered APIs. The foundation model decomposes user requests into API call sequences with appropriate parameters, guided by an API registry providing tool descriptions for selection.

title: TaskMatrix.AI: Completing Tasks by Connecting Foundation Models with Millions of APIs
chunk_text: TaskMatrix.AI automates complex multi-step tasks across digital and physical domains by combining foundation models with specialized APIs. The approach scales as new APIs are registered. Key challenges include API selection accuracy among similar APIs and error propagation in multi-step pipelines.

title: Self-RAG: Learning to Retrieve, Generate, and Critique through Self-Reflection
chunk_text: Self-RAG is a framework that improves a language model's quality and factuality through retrieval and self-reflection. Rather than retrieving a fixed number of passages, the model learns to adaptively retrieve on demand and to critique both retrieved passages and its own generations using special reflection tokens.

title: Self-RAG: Learning to Retrieve, Generate, and Critique through Self-Reflection
chunk_text: Retrieval-augmented generation reduces hallucination but indiscriminate retrieval can introduce irrelevant passages and degrade output. We address whether and when to retrieve, and how to assess retrieved evidence. Self-RAG trains a single model to decide retrieval timing, evaluate passage relevance, and verify whether its output is supported, using reflection tokens generated inline.

title: Self-RAG: Learning to Retrieve, Generate, and Critique through Self-Reflection
chunk_text: Self-RAG outperforms standard RAG and instruction-tuned baselines on open-domain QA, reasoning, and fact verification. Adaptive retrieval with self-critique improves both factuality and citation accuracy. Future work includes extending reflection to longer-form generation and multi-hop retrieval.

title: Active Retrieval Augmented Generation
chunk_text: FLARE is a generation method that actively decides when and what to retrieve during long-form generation. Instead of retrieving once at the start, it anticipates upcoming content by generating a temporary next sentence and retrieving relevant documents whenever the model expresses low confidence.

title: Active Retrieval Augmented Generation
chunk_text: Most RAG systems retrieve once based on the initial query, which is insufficient for long-form generation where information needs shift across the output. We propose forward-looking active retrieval, where the system iteratively predicts the upcoming sentence, uses it as a query when confidence is low, and regenerates with retrieved context.

title: Active Retrieval Augmented Generation
chunk_text: FLARE achieves strong performance across long-form knowledge-intensive generation tasks. Actively triggering retrieval based on generation confidence outperforms single-shot and fixed-interval retrieval. The method generalizes across multiple datasets without task-specific training.

title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Large Language Models: A Survey
chunk_text: This survey reviews the development of retrieval-augmented generation for large language models, organizing the field into naive RAG, advanced RAG, and modular RAG paradigms. It examines the retrieval, generation, and augmentation components and discusses evaluation frameworks and open challenges.

title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Large Language Models: A Survey
chunk_text: Large language models exhibit hallucination and outdated knowledge, which retrieval augmentation mitigates by grounding generation in external sources. We survey the rapidly growing RAG literature, categorize architectures, and analyze how retrieval quality, document chunking, and fusion strategies affect downstream performance.

title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Large Language Models: A Survey
chunk_text: RAG has evolved from simple retrieve-then-read pipelines to modular systems with iterative and adaptive retrieval. Key open problems include retrieval robustness, evaluation methodology, and integration with long-context models. The survey provides a roadmap for future RAG research.

title: REPLUG: Retrieval-Augmented Black-Box Language Models
chunk_text: REPLUG treats the language model as a frozen black box and prepends retrieved documents to the input. A tunable retriever is trained using the language model's own output probabilities as a supervision signal, requiring no access to model internals.

title: REPLUG: Retrieval-Augmented Black-Box Language Models
chunk_text: Many strong language models are available only through APIs, preventing fine-tuning for retrieval augmentation. We ask whether retrieval can improve such black-box models. REPLUG trains the retriever to find documents that minimize the language model's perplexity on the target, aligning retrieval with the frozen model.

title: REPLUG: Retrieval-Augmented Black-Box Language Models
chunk_text: REPLUG improves black-box language model performance on language modeling and downstream tasks without modifying the model. Training the retriever against the model's output distribution is an effective supervision signal. The approach is compatible with arbitrary frozen models.

title: Precise Zero-Shot Dense Retrieval without Relevance Labels
chunk_text: HyDE performs zero-shot dense retrieval by first generating a hypothetical document that answers the query using a language model, then encoding that hypothetical document to retrieve real documents. This sidesteps the need for relevance-labeled training data.

title: Precise Zero-Shot Dense Retrieval without Relevance Labels
chunk_text: Dense retrieval typically requires relevance labels to train query and document encoders, which are unavailable in many settings. We propose generating a hypothetical answer document from the query and using its embedding for retrieval, leveraging the language model to bridge the query-document gap.

title: Precise Zero-Shot Dense Retrieval without Relevance Labels
chunk_text: HyDE matches or exceeds strong supervised dense retrievers across diverse tasks and languages without any relevance labels. Hypothetical document embeddings capture relevance patterns effectively. The method is a practical zero-shot retrieval approach.

title: Corrective Retrieval Augmented Generation
chunk_text: Corrective RAG introduces a lightweight retrieval evaluator that assesses the quality of retrieved documents and triggers corrective actions. When retrieval is judged incorrect or ambiguous, the system falls back to web search and decomposes documents to filter irrelevant content.

title: Corrective Retrieval Augmented Generation
chunk_text: RAG performance degrades sharply when retrieval returns irrelevant documents. We propose evaluating retrieval quality before generation and applying corrective strategies. A retrieval evaluator assigns confidence scores that route the system toward using, discarding, or supplementing retrieved knowledge.

title: Corrective Retrieval Augmented Generation
chunk_text: Corrective RAG improves robustness to retrieval errors across short- and long-form generation tasks. Decoupling retrieval evaluation from generation lets the system recover from poor retrieval. The approach is plug-and-play with existing RAG pipelines.

title: Dense Passage Retrieval for Open-Domain Question Answering
chunk_text: Dense Passage Retrieval learns dense vector representations for questions and passages using a dual-encoder trained on question-passage pairs. It replaces sparse term-matching retrieval such as BM25 with learned dense embeddings for open-domain question answering.

title: Dense Passage Retrieval for Open-Domain Question Answering
chunk_text: Open-domain QA requires retrieving relevant passages from a large corpus. Traditional sparse methods rely on lexical overlap and miss semantic matches. We train a dual-encoder to embed questions and passages into a shared space where relevant pairs are close, enabling efficient maximum inner-product search.

title: Dense Passage Retrieval for Open-Domain Question Answering
chunk_text: Dense Passage Retrieval substantially outperforms BM25 on open-domain QA benchmarks and improves end-to-end answer accuracy. Learned dense representations capture semantic relevance beyond lexical matching. DPR became a foundation for subsequent retrieval-augmented systems.

title: REALM: Retrieval-Augmented Language Model Pre-Training
chunk_text: REALM augments language model pre-training with a learned neural retriever over a textual knowledge corpus. The retriever is trained end-to-end with the language model using masked language modeling as the signal, allowing the model to attend to retrieved documents during prediction.

title: REALM: Retrieval-Augmented Language Model Pre-Training
chunk_text: Language models store knowledge implicitly in parameters, making it hard to interpret or update. We propose learning a knowledge retriever jointly with the language model during pre-training, so the model explicitly retrieves and conditions on documents from a corpus when predicting masked tokens.

title: REALM: Retrieval-Augmented Language Model Pre-Training
chunk_text: REALM improves open-domain QA over models that store knowledge only in parameters. End-to-end training of retrieval with language modeling produces a retriever aligned with the model's needs. Explicit retrieval also improves interpretability and updatability.

title: Atlas: Few-shot Learning with Retrieval Augmented Language Models
chunk_text: Atlas is a retrieval-augmented language model designed for few-shot learning on knowledge-intensive tasks. It jointly trains a dense retriever and a sequence-to-sequence model, achieving strong performance with far fewer parameters than comparable closed-book models.

title: Atlas: Few-shot Learning with Retrieval Augmented Language Models
chunk_text: Large closed-book models memorize knowledge but require enormous scale. We investigate whether retrieval augmentation enables strong few-shot performance at smaller scale. Atlas couples a Contriever-style retriever with a Fusion-in-Decoder reader, training both on few examples.

title: Atlas: Few-shot Learning with Retrieval Augmented Language Models
chunk_text: Atlas matches much larger closed-book models on knowledge-intensive tasks using orders of magnitude fewer parameters. Retrieval augmentation is especially effective in few-shot regimes. Decoupling knowledge storage from reasoning improves parameter efficiency.

title: In-Context Retrieval-Augmented Language Models
chunk_text: In-Context RALM prepends retrieved documents to the input of an off-the-shelf language model without any further training. The work shows that even simple BM25 retrieval combined with frozen models yields substantial language modeling improvements.

title: In-Context Retrieval-Augmented Language Models
chunk_text: Retrieval augmentation often requires specialized training. We study how far one can go by simply prepending retrieved documents to a frozen language model's context. We analyze retrieval frequency, document ranking, and query construction to maximize gains without changing model weights.

title: In-Context Retrieval-Augmented Language Models
chunk_text: In-context retrieval augmentation improves frozen language models across model sizes with no training. Retrieval stride and reranking matter substantially. The simplicity makes the approach broadly applicable to existing models.

title: Improving Language Models by Retrieving from Trillions of Tokens
chunk_text: RETRO enhances language models by retrieving from a database of trillions of tokens via chunked cross-attention. A relatively small model augmented with retrieval matches the performance of much larger models on language modeling.

title: Improving Language Models by Retrieving from Trillions of Tokens
chunk_text: Scaling parameters is an expensive route to better language modeling. We explore scaling retrieval instead. RETRO retrieves nearest-neighbor chunks from a massive text database and integrates them through a chunked cross-attention mechanism interleaved with standard layers.

title: Improving Language Models by Retrieving from Trillions of Tokens
chunk_text: RETRO with retrieval from trillions of tokens matches models 25 times larger on language modeling. Retrieval is a competitive alternative to parameter scaling. The chunked cross-attention design integrates retrieved context efficiently.

title: Leveraging Passage Retrieval with Generative Models for Open Domain Question Answering
chunk_text: Fusion-in-Decoder retrieves multiple passages and processes them independently in the encoder, then fuses their representations in the decoder to generate answers. This allows the model to aggregate evidence across many retrieved passages efficiently.

title: Leveraging Passage Retrieval with Generative Models for Open Domain Question Answering
chunk_text: Generative open-domain QA must combine evidence from many retrieved passages. Concatenating passages is limited by sequence length. We encode each passage separately and let the decoder attend jointly across all encoded passages, scaling to large numbers of retrieved documents.

title: Leveraging Passage Retrieval with Generative Models for Open Domain Question Answering
chunk_text: Fusion-in-Decoder achieves strong open-domain QA performance and scales with the number of retrieved passages. Independent encoding with joint decoding is an efficient evidence aggregation strategy. The architecture became widely adopted in retrieval-augmented QA.

title: Self-Consistency Improves Chain of Thought Reasoning in Language Models
chunk_text: Self-consistency replaces greedy decoding in chain-of-thought prompting with sampling multiple diverse reasoning paths and selecting the most consistent final answer by majority vote. This simple decoding strategy substantially improves reasoning accuracy.

title: Self-Consistency Improves Chain of Thought Reasoning in Language Models
chunk_text: Chain-of-thought prompting elicits step-by-step reasoning but greedy decoding commits to a single path that may contain errors. We hypothesize that complex problems admit multiple valid reasoning paths converging on the same answer. Sampling diverse paths and marginalizing over them should improve robustness.

title: Self-Consistency Improves Chain of Thought Reasoning in Language Models
chunk_text: Self-consistency yields large gains across arithmetic and commonsense reasoning benchmarks. Aggregating multiple sampled reasoning paths is more reliable than any single path. The method requires no additional training or supervision.

title: Least-to-Most Prompting Enables Complex Reasoning in Large Language Models
chunk_text: Least-to-most prompting decomposes a complex problem into a sequence of simpler subproblems and solves them in order, using the answers to earlier subproblems as context for later ones. This enables generalization to harder problems than seen in the prompt.

title: Least-to-Most Prompting Enables Complex Reasoning in Large Language Models
chunk_text: Chain-of-thought struggles to generalize from easy demonstrations to harder problems. We propose explicitly decomposing problems into ordered subproblems. The model first reduces a problem to subproblems, then sequentially solves each, building toward the final answer.

title: Least-to-Most Prompting Enables Complex Reasoning in Large Language Models
chunk_text: Least-to-most prompting solves problems substantially harder than the prompt examples, improving compositional generalization. Explicit decomposition outperforms standard chain-of-thought on symbolic and mathematical reasoning. The two-stage approach is broadly applicable.

title: Graph of Thoughts: Solving Elaborate Problems with Large Language Models
chunk_text: Graph of Thoughts models reasoning as a graph where vertices are intermediate thoughts and edges are dependencies, enabling aggregation, refinement, and feedback loops over thoughts. This generalizes chain and tree structures to arbitrary graphs.

title: Graph of Thoughts: Solving Elaborate Problems with Large Language Models
chunk_text: Tree-of-thoughts allows branching reasoning but cannot merge or refine thoughts arbitrarily. We represent reasoning as a graph, where thoughts can be combined, looped, and distilled. This richer structure supports operations like aggregating partial solutions and iteratively improving them.

title: Graph of Thoughts: Solving Elaborate Problems with Large Language Models
chunk_text: Graph of Thoughts improves solution quality and reduces cost on tasks like sorting and set operations compared to tree-of-thoughts. Graph-structured reasoning enables aggregation and refinement beyond tree branching. The framework is extensible to new thought transformations.

title: PAL: Program-aided Language Models
chunk_text: Program-aided language models generate reasoning steps as executable program code and offload the actual computation to a Python interpreter. This separates reasoning from calculation, eliminating arithmetic errors in the model's output.

title: PAL: Program-aided Language Models
chunk_text: Language models reason in natural language but make arithmetic and logical execution errors. We propose having the model write programs that express the reasoning steps, then execute them with an interpreter. The model focuses on decomposition while the interpreter handles exact computation.

title: PAL: Program-aided Language Models
chunk_text: PAL outperforms chain-of-thought on mathematical and symbolic reasoning by delegating computation to an interpreter. Separating reasoning from execution removes a major error source. The approach generalizes across reasoning tasks requiring precise computation.

title: ReWOO: Decoupling Reasoning from Observations for Efficient Augmented Language Models
chunk_text: ReWOO decouples the reasoning process from external tool observations by generating a complete plan of tool calls upfront, then executing them, then combining results. This reduces redundant LLM calls compared to interleaved reasoning-acting approaches.

title: ReWOO: Decoupling Reasoning from Observations for Efficient Augmented Language Models
chunk_text: Interleaved reasoning-acting agents like ReAct repeatedly feed observations back into the model, incurring high token cost. We propose separating planning from execution: the model produces a full reasoning plan with placeholder evidence, tools fill the placeholders, and a solver combines them.

title: ReWOO: Decoupling Reasoning from Observations for Efficient Augmented Language Models
chunk_text: ReWOO achieves comparable or better accuracy than ReAct while using substantially fewer tokens. Decoupling reasoning from observation reduces redundant context. The modular design also improves robustness to tool failures.

title: Automatic Chain of Thought Prompting in Large Language Models
chunk_text: Auto-CoT automatically constructs chain-of-thought demonstrations by clustering questions and generating reasoning chains for representative examples, removing the need for manually written demonstrations.

title: Automatic Chain of Thought Prompting in Large Language Models
chunk_text: Chain-of-thought prompting requires hand-crafted reasoning demonstrations, which is labor-intensive. We automate demonstration construction by clustering questions for diversity and using zero-shot prompting to generate reasoning chains for cluster representatives, then using these as demonstrations.

title: Automatic Chain of Thought Prompting in Large Language Models
chunk_text: Auto-CoT matches manually designed chain-of-thought prompts across reasoning benchmarks. Diversity-based sampling of demonstrations is key to performance. The method removes manual prompt engineering for chain-of-thought.

title: Measuring and Narrowing the Compositionality Gap in Language Models
chunk_text: This work introduces the self-ask prompting method, where the model explicitly asks and answers follow-up subquestions before producing a final answer. Self-ask narrows the compositionality gap and integrates naturally with a search engine.

title: Measuring and Narrowing the Compositionality Gap in Language Models
chunk_text: Language models often know the facts needed for a multi-hop question yet fail to compose them. We measure this compositionality gap and propose self-ask, where the model decomposes a question into explicit follow-up questions, optionally answered by a search engine, before composing the final answer.

title: Measuring and Narrowing the Compositionality Gap in Language Models
chunk_text: Self-ask improves multi-hop question answering and narrows the compositionality gap. Explicit subquestion decomposition makes reasoning steps inspectable and supports tool integration. The gap persists even as model scale increases.

title: Decomposed Prompting: A Modular Approach for Solving Complex Tasks
chunk_text: Decomposed prompting solves complex tasks by breaking them into subtasks, each handled by a dedicated prompt that can be further decomposed recursively or delegated to specialized handlers including retrieval and symbolic operations.

title: Decomposed Prompting: A Modular Approach for Solving Complex Tasks
chunk_text: Single monolithic prompts struggle with complex compositional tasks. We propose a modular library of decomposition prompts, where a controller routes subtasks to specialized handlers. Handlers can recurse, call other handlers, or invoke external operations, enabling flexible task solving.

title: Decomposed Prompting: A Modular Approach for Solving Complex Tasks
chunk_text: Decomposed prompting outperforms chain-of-thought on tasks requiring compositional and recursive structure. Modular subtask handlers improve reuse and debugging. The approach supports integrating symbolic and retrieval operations into prompting.

title: Gorilla: Large Language Model Connected with Massive APIs
chunk_text: Gorilla is a finetuned language model that generates accurate API calls across large, changing API collections. It uses retrieval-aware training so the model can adapt to documentation changes at inference time and reduce hallucinated API usage.

title: Gorilla: Large Language Model Connected with Massive APIs
chunk_text: Language models struggle to invoke the correct API among thousands of options and hallucinate arguments. We finetune a model with a document retriever in the loop, teaching it to consult retrieved API documentation when generating calls. This handles overlapping and evolving APIs.

title: Gorilla: Large Language Model Connected with Massive APIs
chunk_text: Gorilla outperforms general models including GPT-4 at writing correct API calls and adapts to documentation changes via retrieval. Retrieval-aware training reduces hallucination. The approach scales to large, dynamic tool collections.

title: CRITIC: Large Language Models Can Self-Correct with Tool-Interactive Critiquing
chunk_text: CRITIC enables language models to verify and correct their own outputs by interacting with external tools such as search engines and code interpreters. The model critiques its output using tool feedback, then revises accordingly.

title: CRITIC: Large Language Models Can Self-Correct with Tool-Interactive Critiquing
chunk_text: Language models cannot reliably self-correct using only their internal knowledge. We propose grounding self-correction in external tools: the model generates an output, queries tools to validate it, and uses the returned evidence to critique and revise, mirroring how humans verify claims.

title: CRITIC: Large Language Models Can Self-Correct with Tool-Interactive Critiquing
chunk_text: CRITIC improves accuracy across question answering, mathematical reasoning, and toxicity reduction by grounding self-correction in tools. Tool feedback is more reliable than purely internal critique. External verification is essential for trustworthy self-correction.

title: Chameleon: Plug-and-Play Compositional Reasoning with Large Language Models
chunk_text: Chameleon augments language models with a set of plug-and-play modules including vision models, search engines, and Python functions, composing them into programs to solve multimodal and knowledge-intensive reasoning tasks.

title: Chameleon: Plug-and-Play Compositional Reasoning with Large Language Models
chunk_text: Language models lack access to up-to-date information, precise computation, and visual perception. We build a compositional reasoning system where the LLM acts as a planner that assembles sequences of modules from a toolbox to address each query's specific needs.

title: Chameleon: Plug-and-Play Compositional Reasoning with Large Language Models
chunk_text: Chameleon achieves strong results on science question answering and tabular reasoning by composing heterogeneous tools. LLM-driven program synthesis over a module library is flexible and interpretable. Plug-and-play design eases extension with new tools.

title: RestGPT: Connecting Large Language Models with Real-World RESTful APIs
chunk_text: RestGPT connects language models to real-world RESTful APIs through a coarse-to-fine planning module and an API executor that handles authentication, parameter binding, and response parsing for complex multi-step tasks.

title: RestGPT: Connecting Large Language Models with Real-World RESTful APIs
chunk_text: Real-world APIs are numerous, complex, and return large structured responses that challenge language model agents. We propose a hierarchical planner that decomposes user instructions into API calls and an executor that manages the practical details of invoking RESTful services.

title: RestGPT: Connecting Large Language Models with Real-World RESTful APIs
chunk_text: RestGPT completes complex tasks over real APIs such as movie databases and music services. Coarse-to-fine planning handles API complexity better than flat planning. Robust response parsing is critical for real-world tool use.

title: MemGPT: Towards LLMs as Operating Systems
chunk_text: MemGPT manages a tiered memory hierarchy analogous to an operating system, allowing a language model to page information between a limited context window and external storage. This enables unbounded effective context for long conversations and document analysis.

title: MemGPT: Towards LLMs as Operating Systems
chunk_text: Fixed context windows limit language models on long conversations and large documents. Inspired by operating system memory management, we give the model functions to move data between its context and external storage, letting it decide what to keep in working memory and what to retrieve.

title: MemGPT: Towards LLMs as Operating Systems
chunk_text: MemGPT handles long-term conversation and large-document analysis beyond the native context window. OS-inspired memory paging lets the model manage its own context. Self-directed memory management is a promising direction for long-horizon agents.

title: ExpeL: LLM Agents Are Experiential Learners
chunk_text: ExpeL enables language model agents to learn from experience without parameter updates by collecting trajectories across training tasks, extracting natural-language insights, and retrieving relevant experiences at test time.

title: ExpeL: LLM Agents Are Experiential Learners
chunk_text: Fine-tuning agents is costly and proprietary models cannot be updated. We ask whether agents can improve from experience using only their context. ExpeL gathers successful and failed trajectories, distills cross-task insights, and recalls similar past experiences when facing new tasks.

title: ExpeL: LLM Agents Are Experiential Learners
chunk_text: ExpeL improves agent performance across tasks without any gradient updates. Extracting and retrieving natural-language experience is an effective learning mechanism for frozen models. Experiential learning complements in-context and tool-use approaches.

title: FireAct: Toward Language Agent Fine-tuning
chunk_text: FireAct studies fine-tuning language models for agentic tasks using trajectories generated by stronger models across multiple prompting methods. It shows that fine-tuning on diverse agent trajectories improves smaller models substantially.

title: FireAct: Toward Language Agent Fine-tuning
chunk_text: Most language agents rely on prompting frozen models, leaving fine-tuning underexplored. We investigate fine-tuning agents on trajectories collected from multiple tasks and prompting methods including ReAct and chain-of-thought. We analyze how trajectory diversity affects agent robustness.

title: FireAct: Toward Language Agent Fine-tuning
chunk_text: Fine-tuning on diverse agent trajectories improves smaller models' performance and robustness over prompting alone. Mixing prompting methods during fine-tuning helps generalization. Agent fine-tuning is a promising complement to prompting-based agents.

title: AgentVerse: Facilitating Multi-Agent Collaboration and Exploring Emergent Behaviors
chunk_text: AgentVerse is a framework for orchestrating multiple language model agents through expert recruitment, collaborative decision-making, action execution, and evaluation phases. It studies emergent social behaviors among collaborating agents.

title: AgentVerse: Facilitating Multi-Agent Collaboration and Exploring Emergent Behaviors
chunk_text: Coordinating multiple agents toward a shared goal requires structured collaboration. We propose a framework that dynamically recruits expert agents, conducts collaborative decision-making, executes actions, and evaluates outcomes in iterative rounds, while observing emergent cooperative and competitive behaviors.

title: AgentVerse: Facilitating Multi-Agent Collaboration and Exploring Emergent Behaviors
chunk_text: AgentVerse enables multi-agent groups to outperform individual agents on reasoning and coding tasks. Structured collaboration phases improve coordination. The framework surfaces emergent behaviors relevant to multi-agent system design.

title: Improving Factuality and Reasoning in Language Models through Multiagent Debate
chunk_text: This work has multiple language model instances propose and debate their individual responses over several rounds, converging on a shared answer. Multiagent debate improves factual accuracy and reasoning over single-model baselines.

title: Improving Factuality and Reasoning in Language Models through Multiagent Debate
chunk_text: A single language model may commit to flawed reasoning. We propose having multiple model instances independently answer, then critique and revise their answers in light of others' responses across debate rounds. This mirrors deliberative human reasoning and surfaces errors.

title: Improving Factuality and Reasoning in Language Models through Multiagent Debate
chunk_text: Multiagent debate improves factuality and reasoning across diverse tasks. Iterative cross-examination among model instances reduces errors and hallucination. Debate is a simple, training-free way to improve output quality.

title: MetaAgents: Simulating Interactions of Human Behaviors for LLM-based Task-oriented Coordination
chunk_text: MetaAgents studies coordination among language model agents in simulated task-oriented social environments, examining how agents with different roles negotiate, plan, and assign tasks to achieve collective goals.

title: MetaAgents: Simulating Interactions of Human Behaviors for LLM-based Task-oriented Coordination
chunk_text: Coordinating language model agents in realistic social settings remains challenging. We construct a simulated environment where agents with distinct roles must communicate and divide labor. We analyze how reasoning and coordination capabilities affect collective task success.

title: MetaAgents: Simulating Interactions of Human Behaviors for LLM-based Task-oriented Coordination
chunk_text: MetaAgents reveals both capabilities and limitations of language model agents in coordinated task-oriented settings. Role specialization and communication structure strongly affect outcomes. Coordination remains a bottleneck for complex multi-agent tasks.

title: RoCo: Dialectic Multi-Robot Collaboration with Large Language Models
chunk_text: RoCo uses language models for multi-robot collaboration, where each robot agent reasons and dialogues to jointly plan, then validates the plan against motion constraints. It combines high-level language reasoning with low-level motion planning.

title: RoCo: Dialectic Multi-Robot Collaboration with Large Language Models
chunk_text: Coordinating multiple robots requires both high-level task allocation and low-level feasibility. We assign each robot a language model agent that proposes and discusses subtask plans through dialogue, then validate the agreed plan with a motion planner, iterating when validation fails.

title: RoCo: Dialectic Multi-Robot Collaboration with Large Language Models
chunk_text: RoCo achieves effective multi-robot coordination across collaborative manipulation tasks. Combining dialectic language reasoning with motion validation bridges high- and low-level planning. Language-based negotiation is a viable coordination mechanism for embodied multi-agent systems.

title: GAIA: A Benchmark for General AI Assistants
chunk_text: GAIA is a benchmark of real-world questions requiring reasoning, multimodality, web browsing, and tool use. The questions are conceptually simple for humans yet challenging for AI assistants, testing fundamental assistant capabilities.

title: GAIA: A Benchmark for General AI Assistants
chunk_text: Existing benchmarks saturate or test narrow skills. We propose questions that humans answer easily but that require AI assistants to combine reasoning, tool use, and multimodal understanding. The benchmark resists memorization and measures general assistant competence.

title: GAIA: A Benchmark for General AI Assistants
chunk_text: GAIA exposes a large gap between human and AI-assistant performance despite question simplicity for humans. Tool use and multi-step reasoning remain bottlenecks. The benchmark provides a target for general-purpose assistant development.

title: WebArena: A Realistic Web Environment for Building Autonomous Agents
chunk_text: WebArena is a realistic, reproducible web environment with functional websites for e-commerce, forums, and collaborative development, paired with tasks that require agents to perform multi-step actions to achieve goals.

title: WebArena: A Realistic Web Environment for Building Autonomous Agents
chunk_text: Evaluating web agents requires realistic environments rather than simplified simulations. We build self-hosted functional websites and define long-horizon tasks with execution-based evaluation. This enables reproducible measurement of agent capabilities in web navigation and interaction.

title: WebArena: A Realistic Web Environment for Building Autonomous Agents
chunk_text: WebArena shows that current language model agents complete only a small fraction of realistic web tasks. Long-horizon planning and robust action execution are key gaps. The environment supports reproducible web-agent research.

title: SWE-bench: Can Language Models Resolve Real-World GitHub Issues?
chunk_text: SWE-bench evaluates language models on resolving real GitHub issues by generating code patches that must pass the repository's test suite. The tasks require understanding large codebases and coordinating changes across files.

title: SWE-bench: Can Language Models Resolve Real-World GitHub Issues?
chunk_text: Code generation benchmarks use isolated functions, not realistic software engineering. We collect real issue-and-pull-request pairs from popular repositories, requiring models to produce patches validated by the project's own tests. This measures practical software engineering ability.

title: SWE-bench: Can Language Models Resolve Real-World GitHub Issues?
chunk_text: SWE-bench reveals that even strong models resolve only a small percentage of real issues. Repository-scale context and cross-file coordination are major challenges. The benchmark drives research on practical coding agents.

title: MINT: Evaluating LLMs in Multi-turn Interaction with Tools and Language Feedback
chunk_text: MINT evaluates language models on multi-turn tasks where they can use tools and receive natural-language feedback. It measures how well models leverage tool calls and incorporate user feedback across interaction turns.

title: MINT: Evaluating LLMs in Multi-turn Interaction with Tools and Language Feedback
chunk_text: Real assistant use involves multiple turns, tool use, and iterative feedback, but most benchmarks are single-turn. We construct tasks that allow tool interaction and simulated user feedback, measuring how performance changes as models use more turns and feedback.

title: MINT: Evaluating LLMs in Multi-turn Interaction with Tools and Language Feedback
chunk_text: MINT shows that models vary widely in their ability to use tools and feedback across turns, and that some improvements from feedback do not generalize. Multi-turn tool interaction is an important and under-measured capability. The benchmark guides development of interactive agents.

title: Plan-and-Solve Prompting: Improving Zero-Shot Chain-of-Thought Reasoning
chunk_text: Plan-and-Solve prompting first devises a plan to divide a task into subtasks, then carries out the subtasks, reducing calculation and missing-step errors in zero-shot reasoning.

title: Plan-and-Solve Prompting: Improving Zero-Shot Chain-of-Thought Reasoning
chunk_text: We address common error types in zero-shot chain-of-thought by explicitly prompting the model to plan before solving.

title: Plan-and-Solve Prompting: Improving Zero-Shot Chain-of-Thought Reasoning
chunk_text: Planning before solving reduces reasoning errors without exemplars.

title: ART: Automatic Multi-Step Reasoning and Tool-Use for Large Language Models
chunk_text: ART automatically selects reasoning demonstrations and interleaves tool calls during multi-step reasoning, allowing frozen LLMs to use external tools without hand-crafted prompts.

title: ART: Automatic Multi-Step Reasoning and Tool-Use for Large Language Models
chunk_text: We automate program-style multi-step reasoning with tool use for frozen language models.

title: ART: Automatic Multi-Step Reasoning and Tool-Use for Large Language Models
chunk_text: Automatic reasoning programs with tool use generalize across tasks and tools.

title: Chain-of-Verification Reduces Hallucination in Large Language Models
chunk_text: Chain-of-Verification drafts an initial response, plans verification questions, answers them independently, and produces a verified final response, reducing factual hallucination.

title: Chain-of-Verification Reduces Hallucination in Large Language Models
chunk_text: We reduce hallucination by having the model verify its own claims through independently answered checking questions.

title: Chain-of-Verification Reduces Hallucination in Large Language Models
chunk_text: Self-verification through planned questions reduces hallucinations in generated text.

title: Reinforced Self-Training (ReST) for Language Modeling
chunk_text: ReST alternates generating a dataset from the policy (Grow) and fine-tuning on filtered high-reward samples (Improve), an offline RL approach for aligning language models.

title: Reinforced Self-Training (ReST) for Language Modeling
chunk_text: We align language models with reward signals through an offline grow-and-improve self-training loop.

title: Reinforced Self-Training (ReST) for Language Modeling
chunk_text: Reinforced self-training improves quality with reduced compute relative to online RL.

title: WebShop: Towards Scalable Real-World Web Interaction with Grounded Language Agents
chunk_text: WebShop is a simulated e-commerce environment with millions of products where agents must navigate and purchase items from natural-language instructions, testing grounded web interaction.

title: WebShop: Towards Scalable Real-World Web Interaction with Grounded Language Agents
chunk_text: We build a large-scale web environment to train and evaluate language agents on realistic shopping tasks.

title: WebShop: Towards Scalable Real-World Web Interaction with Grounded Language Agents
chunk_text: Grounded web agents show progress but remain far below human performance on realistic tasks.

title: Mind2Web: Towards a Generalist Agent for the Web
chunk_text: Mind2Web is a dataset for developing generalist web agents that follow language instructions to complete tasks across many real websites and domains.

title: Mind2Web: Towards a Generalist Agent for the Web
chunk_text: We collect diverse real-website tasks to train and evaluate generalist web-browsing agents.

title: Mind2Web: Towards a Generalist Agent for the Web
chunk_text: Generalist web agents require broad transfer across sites, domains, and interaction patterns.

title: CogAgent: A Visual Language Model for GUI Agents
chunk_text: CogAgent is a vision-language model specialized for GUI understanding and navigation, recognizing screen elements and predicting actions from screenshots.

title: CogAgent: A Visual Language Model for GUI Agents
chunk_text: We build a visual language model that operates graphical user interfaces directly from pixels.

title: CogAgent: A Visual Language Model for GUI Agents
chunk_text: Screen-grounded visual agents can navigate GUIs without relying on accessibility trees.

title: AppAgent: Multimodal Agents as Smartphone Users
chunk_text: AppAgent is a multimodal agent that learns to operate smartphone applications by exploration and by observing demonstrations, acting through taps and swipes.

title: AppAgent: Multimodal Agents as Smartphone Users
chunk_text: We develop a multimodal agent that uses mobile apps the way a human user would.

title: AppAgent: Multimodal Agents as Smartphone Users
chunk_text: Exploration-based learning enables agents to operate unfamiliar smartphone applications.

title: Ghost in the Minecraft: Generally Capable Agents for Open-World Environments
chunk_text: Ghost in the Minecraft combines LLM-based planning with structured action interfaces to achieve long-horizon goals in the open-world game Minecraft.

title: Ghost in the Minecraft: Generally Capable Agents for Open-World Environments
chunk_text: We pair language-model planning with a structured action layer for open-world embodied tasks.

title: Ghost in the Minecraft: Generally Capable Agents for Open-World Environments
chunk_text: Structured LLM planning unlocks long-horizon achievement in open-world environments.

title: Describe, Explain, Plan and Select: Interactive Planning with LLMs for Open-World Agents
chunk_text: DEPS is an interactive planning approach where an LLM describes, explains failures, plans, and selects goals, improving long-horizon task completion for open-world agents.

title: Describe, Explain, Plan and Select: Interactive Planning with LLMs for Open-World Agents
chunk_text: We propose an interactive describe-explain-plan-select loop for robust open-world planning.

title: Describe, Explain, Plan and Select: Interactive Planning with LLMs for Open-World Agents
chunk_text: Failure-aware interactive planning improves long-horizon success rates.

title: Do As I Can, Not As I Say: Grounding Language in Robotic Affordances (SayCan)
chunk_text: SayCan grounds language-model instructions in robotic affordances by combining LLM task likelihoods with learned value functions, so a robot performs feasible useful actions.

title: Do As I Can, Not As I Say: Grounding Language in Robotic Affordances (SayCan)
chunk_text: We ground language-model plans in what a robot can actually do via affordance value functions.

title: Do As I Can, Not As I Say: Grounding Language in Robotic Affordances (SayCan)
chunk_text: Combining language priors with affordances yields feasible real-robot behavior.

title: Inner Monologue: Embodied Reasoning through Planning with Language Models
chunk_text: Inner Monologue incorporates environment feedback into an LLM planning loop, letting embodied agents replan from success detection, scene description, and human feedback.

title: Inner Monologue: Embodied Reasoning through Planning with Language Models
chunk_text: We close the loop between language-model planning and embodied feedback.

title: Inner Monologue: Embodied Reasoning through Planning with Language Models
chunk_text: Feedback-grounded inner monologue improves embodied task completion.

title: Code as Policies: Language Model Programs for Embodied Control
chunk_text: Code as Policies uses LLMs to write executable robot policy code from language commands, composing perception and control APIs into runnable programs.

title: Code as Policies: Language Model Programs for Embodied Control
chunk_text: We treat robot control as program synthesis driven by language models.

title: Code as Policies: Language Model Programs for Embodied Control
chunk_text: Language-model-generated policy code generalizes to new instructions and objects.

title: Language Agent Tree Search Unifies Reasoning, Acting, and Planning
chunk_text: LATS uses Monte Carlo tree search over language-agent actions with environment feedback and self-reflection, unifying reasoning, acting, and planning.

title: Language Agent Tree Search Unifies Reasoning, Acting, and Planning
chunk_text: We bring principled search to language agents via Monte Carlo tree search with reflection.

title: Language Agent Tree Search Unifies Reasoning, Acting, and Planning
chunk_text: Search over agent actions improves decision-making on reasoning and tool-use tasks.

title: Reasoning with Language Model is Planning with World Model (RAP)
chunk_text: RAP repurposes an LLM as both a reasoning agent and a world model, using Monte Carlo tree search to plan over predicted states for multi-step reasoning.

title: Reasoning with Language Model is Planning with World Model (RAP)
chunk_text: We cast reasoning as planning by treating the language model as a world model.

title: Reasoning with Language Model is Planning with World Model (RAP)
chunk_text: Planning with an LLM world model improves multi-step reasoning.

title: ADaPT: As-Needed Decomposition and Planning with Language Models
chunk_text: ADaPT recursively decomposes tasks only when the executor fails, adapting plan granularity to task and model capability for interactive decision-making.

title: ADaPT: As-Needed Decomposition and Planning with Language Models
chunk_text: We decompose tasks as needed rather than all at once, adapting to failures.

title: ADaPT: As-Needed Decomposition and Planning with Language Models
chunk_text: As-needed recursive decomposition improves success on complex interactive tasks.

title: AgentTuning: Enabling Generalized Agent Abilities for LLMs
chunk_text: AgentTuning instruction-tunes open LLMs on a mixture of agent trajectories and general instructions, improving agent abilities without sacrificing general capability.

title: AgentTuning: Enabling Generalized Agent Abilities for LLMs
chunk_text: We fine-tune open models on agent interaction data to build generalist agents.

title: AgentTuning: Enabling Generalized Agent Abilities for LLMs
chunk_text: Mixed agent and general tuning yields broad agent skills while preserving general ability.

title: Lemur: Harmonizing Natural Language and Code for Language Agents
chunk_text: Lemur is an open model pretrained and instruction-tuned to balance language and coding ability, targeting the needs of language agents that act in environments.

title: Lemur: Harmonizing Natural Language and Code for Language Agents
chunk_text: We build open models that harmonize natural language and code for agentic use.

title: Lemur: Harmonizing Natural Language and Code for Language Agents
chunk_text: Balanced language-code ability improves agent performance across environments.

title: Interleaving Retrieval with Chain-of-Thought Reasoning for Multi-Step Questions (IRCoT)
chunk_text: IRCoT interleaves retrieval with chain-of-thought, using each reasoning step to guide what to retrieve next, improving multi-hop question answering.

title: Interleaving Retrieval with Chain-of-Thought Reasoning for Multi-Step Questions (IRCoT)
chunk_text: We couple retrieval and reasoning so each guides the other for multi-hop QA.

title: Interleaving Retrieval with Chain-of-Thought Reasoning for Multi-Step Questions (IRCoT)
chunk_text: Interleaving retrieval with reasoning outperforms one-shot retrieval on multi-hop questions.

title: Demonstrate-Search-Predict: Composing Retrieval and Language Models for Knowledge-Intensive NLP
chunk_text: DSP is a framework that composes retrieval models and language models through programs that demonstrate, search, and predict, for knowledge-intensive tasks.

title: Demonstrate-Search-Predict: Composing Retrieval and Language Models for Knowledge-Intensive NLP
chunk_text: We compose retrievers and language models with a programming abstraction for knowledge tasks.

title: Demonstrate-Search-Predict: Composing Retrieval and Language Models for Knowledge-Intensive NLP
chunk_text: Program-level composition of retrieval and generation improves knowledge-intensive QA.

title: DSPy: Compiling Declarative Language Model Calls into Self-Improving Pipelines
chunk_text: DSPy expresses LLM pipelines as declarative modules and compiles them by optimizing prompts and demonstrations, replacing brittle hand-crafted prompting.

title: DSPy: Compiling Declarative Language Model Calls into Self-Improving Pipelines
chunk_text: We treat LLM pipelines as programs that can be optimized and compiled.

title: DSPy: Compiling Declarative Language Model Calls into Self-Improving Pipelines
chunk_text: Declarative, compilable pipelines outperform hand-tuned prompting.

title: Chain-of-Note: Enhancing Robustness in Retrieval-Augmented Language Models
chunk_text: Chain-of-Note generates sequential reading notes for retrieved documents to assess relevance before answering, improving robustness to noisy or irrelevant retrieval.

title: Chain-of-Note: Enhancing Robustness in Retrieval-Augmented Language Models
chunk_text: We add a note-taking step over retrieved documents to improve RAG robustness.

title: Chain-of-Note: Enhancing Robustness in Retrieval-Augmented Language Models
chunk_text: Reading notes improve robustness to irrelevant or noisy retrieved passages.

title: RECOMP: Improving Retrieval-Augmented LMs with Compression and Selective Augmentation
chunk_text: RECOMP compresses retrieved documents into concise summaries before in-context augmentation, reducing cost and filtering irrelevant content.

title: RECOMP: Improving Retrieval-Augmented LMs with Compression and Selective Augmentation
chunk_text: We compress retrieved evidence into summaries to make RAG cheaper and more focused.

title: RECOMP: Improving Retrieval-Augmented LMs with Compression and Selective Augmentation
chunk_text: Compressing retrieved context improves efficiency without harming task performance.

title: Query2doc: Query Expansion with Large Language Models
chunk_text: Query2doc expands a query by prompting an LLM to generate a pseudo-document, which improves both sparse and dense retrieval.

title: Query2doc: Query Expansion with Large Language Models
chunk_text: We expand queries with LLM-generated pseudo-documents to improve retrieval.

title: Query2doc: Query Expansion with Large Language Models
chunk_text: LLM-based query expansion consistently improves retrieval effectiveness.

title: Generate rather than Retrieve: Large Language Models are Strong Context Generators
